subject: Hosted API public phrasing: data movement & subcontractor language

From: Andrea King <andrea.king@acmecloud.com>

Cc:

Subject: Hosted API — requests for public-facing wording on data movement and subcontractors

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising. Procurement and legal here at Acme Cloud have a short set of public-language questions we need to present to our security review board. We've attached a short matrix (Acme_Questions_DataMovement.xlsx) with a handful of items.

High level asks:
- Short (1–2 sentence) descriptions we can show on our vendor list for: how data can move (cross-border), whether Redwood uses subprocessors, and where customers can find an up-to-date list of subprocessors.
- A clear statement about whether customer payloads are ever sent to third-party analytics, and whether model variants might route inference to other regions.
- Suggested microcopy for the Hosted API console privacy/help tooltip (two variants: plain-language and more technical).

Could you provide a short set of candidate snippets we can paste into our vendor intake form by EOD Thursday (US PST)? Procurement will do an initial pass and then follow with a SOC2 evidence request if the language is acceptable.

Thanks — Andrea
Andrea King

Andrea — thanks for the clear matrix. Attaching a first-pass phrasebank (redwood_public_phrasebank_v1.docx) with short and slightly more technical options for each item you called out.

Quick summary of what you'll find inside:
- "What we may do with data": two 1–2 sentence options (consumer-facing / technical).
- "Subprocessors and where to find them": a concise line that links to our subprocessors page + a fallback "how we notify customers" line.
- "Cross-border transfers": plain-language summary + a short note about standard contractual safeguards where relevant.
- "Console tooltip copy": two 1-line snippets: one <100 char, one ~200 char.

Marissa — can you glance for tone (customer-facing) and push edits if needed?
Kimberly — can you review for legal accuracy (esp. the transfer & subprocessor link language)? We tried to avoid commitments about specific regions for model execution; noted as "may be routed to a compatible region" in the technical variant.

Andrea, if this looks reasonable at a glance, let me know which variant you prefer and we'll finalize before your procurement pass.

Best,

Vanessa — thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed redwood_public_phrasebank_v1 and added inline edits / comments. Key points for Andrea/procurement:

1) Subprocessor list link: we should link to a live public page and include a one-line description of update cadence (eg: "updated monthly"). Avoid wording that implies we will notify every customer individually unless that's part of a contract addendum.

2) Cross-border language: technical variant should reference safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) where applicable, but the plain-language snippet must not promise specific legal mechanisms — instead say "where required by law, we rely on standard safeguards to protect data moved across borders."

3) Analytics/telemetry: we must be explicit that customer payloads are not shipped to third-party analytics vendors for model training. We do collect aggregate telemetry for performance/ops (latency, error rates) and that should be stated separately.

4) Regions/model execution: we shouldn't promise that a particular model will run only in a given region unless customer has a Dedicated or Private deployment. For Hosted API customers we can commit to region-routing policies (configurable by customer) but not absolute locality for all hosted variants — suggested phrasing included.

I've attached a short redlined snippet below (extracted from the doc). Please incorporate and send the consolidated version back to Andrea. Happy to sign off once Marissa confirms tone.

Andrea — attaching the consolidated snippet set and a link to the live subprocessors page (see doc link). Below are the two short options we recommend for your vendor intake form.

OPTION A (plain-language, consumer-facing):
"Redwood processes requests to our Hosted API to produce outputs for your application. We may route processing to data centers in other countries; where required by law we rely on standard safeguards to protect data moved across borders. We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors and security controls at the link below. We do not share customer payloads with third-party analytics vendors for model training."

OPTION B (technical/concise):
"Requests to Redwood's Hosted API may be processed in compatible regions and, where applicable, rely on standard contractual safeguards for cross-border transfers. An up-to-date subprocessors list and notification procedure are available publicly. Aggregated service telemetry is collected for performance and reliability; customer payloads are not used for third-party analytics or model training without customer consent or contract."

Marissa — can you confirm tone for OPTION A?
Kimberly — your edits are included; if comfortable, I'll send these as a single-page paste to procurement and Andrea's security board.

Andrea — if either option is acceptable, tell us which one and we'll return a final single-page PDF and the evidence pointers (SOC2 report link, subprocessor page, KMS/HSM description) by Monday. If procurement needs earlier turnaround, we can accelerate.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
